title: The New Device Alert
intro: After tonight, every message might look like a scam. Mirage hopes so.
This text came right after you logged in to Zelvora on your new tablet.

notify.text: New device signed in. Was this you?

screen.context: You signed in to Zelvora on a new tablet two minutes ago.

msg.text: Zelvora: a new device signed in to your account.
Was this you? If so, nothing to do.
If it wasn't you, open the Zelvora app and use Account > Security to lock your account.
We will never ask for your password, codes or recovery phrase.

says.label: Matches what you just did
says.lens: It mentions a new device, and you really did just sign in on one.
says.why: A message that matches something you just did is a good sign. Still never click through it.

ask.label: "Was this you?" with nothing to do
ask.lens: If it was you, it asks for nothing.
ask.why: Honest alerts do not demand anything from you.

app.label: Sends you to the app
app.lens: You are told to open the app yourself.
app.why: This is how real platforms tell you to check: through the app you already trust.

never.label: Warns about scams
never.lens: The text says staff never ask for passwords, codes or your phrase.
never.why: Real companies warn you about scams.

sender.label: Sender name
sender.lens: The sender shows Zelvora, in the same thread as your earlier codes.
sender.why: A name alone proves little, but here the thread and the timing agree.

time.label: Sent right after you signed in
time.lens: It arrived two minutes after your sign-in.
time.why: Timing that fits your own actions is reassuring.

actions.label: It was me. Nothing to do

go_ahead.line: It was you, and the alert asked for nothing. You stayed calm and did the right thing: nothing.

block_report.line: That was the real alert. When every message looks like a scam, you may miss the day a real one matters.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real alert about your own sign-in.

what_if.block_report: It matched what you had just done, asked for nothing and sent you to the app. Those are honest signs.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring it was fine because you knew it was you. Had it been a surprise, the app would be the place to check.

golden_rule: Not every alert is a scam. An honest one fits what you did, asks for nothing, and points you to your own app.

quick_check.q: Right after you sign in on a new device, a text says "New device signed in. Was this you?" It has no link and asks for nothing. What is it most likely?

options.text: A scam, all alerts are scams
A reason to share your code

quick_check.explain: It matches your action, has no link and asks for nothing. Honest alerts look calm like this.

hints.nudge: Does it ask you to click, hurry or share anything?
